1192:
(a) Decisions of the Paulding County Marshal's Office that adversely affect or aggrieve any applicant or occupation tax certificate holder under this article may, within five business days, be appealed to the chief marshal. Any applicant or occupation tax certificate holder who is aggrieved or adversely affected by a final decision of the chief marshal or any applicant or permit holder who is aggrieved or adversely affected by a final decision of the chief marshal may request an appeal to the Paulding County Board of Commissioners. Provided however, no variances from the minimum requirements contained in this article shall be granted or considered. Such appeal shall be by written petition, filed in the office of the chief marshal along with a $500.00 appeal fee and be within 15 days after the final decision.
(b) A hearing shall be conducted on each appeal within 30 days after the date of filing the written petition, unless a continuance of such hearing is agreed to by the appellant and chief marshal or as requested by the county attorney or necessary as a result of scheduling issues for the Paulding County Board of Commissioners. However, in no circumstances shall a hearing be more than 90 days after the date of filing of the written petition for appeal. The appellant at such hearing shall have the right to be represented by an attorney, at the expense of the appellant, and to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses. Said appeal hearing before the board of commissioners may be held as part of a special called meeting. At the conclusion of the hearing, the board of commissioners shall issue a decision within 15 days.
(c) The findings of the Paulding County Board of Commissioners shall be forwarded to the chief marshal after the conclusion of the hearing. It shall be the duty of the chief marshal to notify the appellant of the action of the board in writing.
(d) The findings of the Paulding County Board of Commissioners shall not be set aside unless found to be (1) contrary to law or ordinances or (2) unsupported by the evidence on the records as a whole or (3) is arbitrary and unreasonable.
(e) The findings of the Paulding County Board of Commissioners, shall be final unless appealed by filing a petition for review in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 5-3-1 et seq. An aggrieved party shall have all other remedies provided by law or at equity to all ordinances.
(Res. No. 07-31, § 1(Exh. A), 6-26-2007; Res. No. 10-08, § 11, 5-25-2010; Ord. No. 23-10, § 1 (Exh. A), 9-12-2023, eff. 7-1-2023)
1193:
Each business and individual operating under the provisions of this article shall be subject to audit by an independent certified public accountant at the business or operator's expense upon reasonable notice by the chief marshal. Further, the county shall have the right to inspect financial and other records of the operator at any time upon reasonable notice by the Paulding County Comptroller.
(Res. No. 07-31, § 1(Exh. A), 6-26-2007; Res. No. 10-08, § 12, 5-25-2010)
1194:
In addition to any other requirements with respect to the issuance of occupational tax certificates found elsewhere in this Code of Ordinances, the following requirements apply to taxicab businesses having a verifiable dispatch location and/or office location within unincorporated Paulding County:
(1) An applicant for an occupational tax certificate is required to provide information showing its qualifications on a form(s) provided by the Paulding County Marshal's Office.
(2) Applicants must be approved by the chief marshal or designee, and such clearance shall include a background investigation and fingerprinting of the applicant.
(3) No taxicab occupational tax certificate shall be issued to any taxicab business owning or leasing less than eight vehicles unless such business permit is presented and accepted pursuant to reciprocity procedures set forth in subsection (7) below.
(4) All certificates required by the provisions of this article shall expire on the same date as the expiration of the occupation tax certificate.
(5) If the applicant is not a sole proprietor or individual then all partners, officers or managers of the legal entity shall be required to comply with the provisions of this section.
(6) All applicants must:
a. Be at least 21 years of age;
b. Be a citizen of the United States or a legal alien admitted for permanent residence or who has otherwise been granted employment authorization by the United States Immigration and Naturalization Service (who can show proper paperwork therefor).
c. Have not been convicted, been on probation, parole, or been imprisoned for a period of ten years previous to the date of application, for the violation of any of the following offenses of the State of Georgia, or any other state, or of the United States: any felony; driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol; child molestation, criminal solicitation to commit any of the offenses listed in this subsection; attempt to commit any of the offenses listed in this subsection; any misdemeanor crime of violence or theft, any misdemeanor crime of possession, sale or distribution of illegal drugs or any crime involving moral turpitude. Discharge without court adjudication of guilt pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 42-8-62 (First Offender Status) shall not disqualify an applicant from applying for a permit;
d. Provide a verifiable dispatch location staffed by business agents or employees and have a published telephone number;
e. File applications for the initial permitting and inspection of the taxicabs, with a list of all drivers that will be scheduled for driver permitting, indicating whether drivers are business employees or contract drivers. A copy of each contract driver's insurance coverage must be included in the application;
f. Provide a copy of the applicant's rate schedule and the daily hours of operation; and
g. Provide the name, address and telephone number of a responsible individual residing in Paulding County who will be the registered agent for the purpose of service of process or receipt of citations.
(7) In lieu of meeting the requirements set forth in subsection (6) of this section, an applicant for an occupational tax certificate may present to the Paulding County Marshal's Office a current business permit authorizing the applicant to conduct business in another jurisdiction of this state. Upon presentation of same, the marshal's office shall verify the authenticity of same, and if the business permit is valid, shall assess the appropriate occupational tax for the applicant's in county dispatch location or office and issue an occupational tax certificate upon receipt of payment of same.
(Res. No. 07-31, § 1(Exh. A), 6-26-2007; Res. No. 08-06, § 1, 2-28-2008; Res. No. 09-12, § 2, 9-14-2009; Res. No. 10-08, § 13, 5-25-2010)
1195:
(a) An applicant for a business permit is required to provide information showing its qualifications on a form(s) provided by the marshal's office.
(b) Applicants must be approved by the marshal's office or designee, and such clearance shall be included a background investigation and fingerprinting of the applicant.
(c) No business permit shall be issued to any business owning or leasing less vehicles than required under section 70-77A, unless a business permit from another jurisdiction of the State of Georgia is presented and accepted pursuant to subsection (h) of this section.
(d) No business permit shall be issued to an applicant unless the applicant has a valid and current occupation tax certificate to do business issued by a city, county, or consolidated government in the State of Georgia.
(e) All permits required by the provisions of this article shall expire on the same date as the expiration of the occupation tax certificate.
(f) If the applicant is not a sole proprietor or individual then all partners, officers or managers of the legal entity shall be required to comply with the provisions of this section.
(g) All applicants must:
(1) Be at least 21 years of age;
(2) Be a citizen of the United States or a legal alien admitted for permanent residence or who has otherwise been granted employment authorization by the United States Immigration and Naturalization Service (who can show proper paperwork therefor).
(3) Have not been convicted, been on probation, parole, or been imprisoned for a period of ten years previous to the date of application, for the violation of any of the following offenses of the State of Georgia, of any other state, or of the United States: any felony; driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol; criminal solicitation to commit any of the offenses listed in this subsection; attempt to commit any of the offenses listed in this subsection; any misdemeanor crime of violence or theft, any misdemeanor crime of possession, sale or distribution of illegal drugs or any crime involving moral turpitude. Discharge without court adjudication of guilt pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 42-8-62 shall not disqualify an applicant from applying for a permit;
(4) Provide a verifiably dispatch location staffed by business agents or employees and have a published telephone number;
(5) File applications for the initial permitting and inspection of the taxicabs, with a list of all drivers that will be scheduled for driver permitting, indicating whether drivers are business employees or contract drivers. A copy of each contract driver's insurance coverage must be included in the application;
(6) Provide a copy of the applicant's rate schedule and the daily hours of operation; and
(7) Provide the name, address and telephone number of a responsible individual residing in Paulding County who will be the registered agent for the purpose of service of proves or receipt of citations.
(h) In lieu of meeting the requirements set forth in subsection (g) of this section, an applicant for a business permit may present to the Paulding County Marshal's Office a current business permit authorizing the applicant to conduct business in another jurisdiction of this state. Upon presentation of same, the marshal's office shall verify the authenticity of same, and if the business permit is valid, shall give reciprocal recognition to the permit and accept the business permit for filing with the county.
(Res. No. 07-31, § 1(Exh. A), 6-26-2007; Res. No. 08-06, § 2, 2-28-2008; Res. No. 09-12, § 3, 9-14-2009)
1196:
(a) All businesses and drivers permitted pursuant to the provisions of this article shall provide with their application, and shall maintain for the duration of the permit, a certificate of insurance showing proof of motor vehicle insurance covering public liability and property damage issued by a state approved insurer. Such insurance shall insure passengers and third persons against personal injury and property damage in amounts specified by this section.
(b) Except as provided for in subsection (c) below, all businesses and drivers permitted pursuant to the provisions of this article shall provide with their application, and shall maintain for the duration of the permit, motor vehicle insurance coverage per vehicle as required by Georgia state law in the minimum amounts as set forth below:
(1) Minimum insurance coverage for vehicles other than vehicles to be used as limousines is as follows:
a. Coverage in the amount of $100,000.00 for bodily injury, per person;
b. Coverage in the amount of $300,000.00 for bodily injury, per occurrence;
c. Coverage in the amount of $100,000.00 for property damage and
d. Coverage in the amount of $50,000.00 for personal injury protection or medical payment coverage.
(2) Any and all vehicles for limousine service shall provide a minimum coverage in the following sums:
a. Coverage in the amount of $100,000.00 for bodily injury, per person;
b. Coverage in the amount of $500,000.00 for bodily injury, per occurrence;
c. Coverage in the amount of $100,000.00 for property damage and
d. Coverage in the amount of $50,000.00 for personal injury protection or medical payment coverage.
(c) In the event a business or permit holder has been given reciprocal recognition of a valid business permit from another jurisdiction, then the minimum insurance coverages for insurance policies set forth above shall not apply. Provided however, such businesses must in the alternative, provide to the marshal's office a copy of its existing policy with the applicable limits thereon as set forth in subsection (d) below.
(d) All permit holders must provide the Paulding County Marshal's Office or its designee with an annual certificate of insurance showing the existence of such policies of insurance as required by this article. The annual certificate of insurance must be provided to the marshal's office or its designee at least 30 days prior to the expiration of any such insurance. County reserves right to verify insurance coverage at any time and to take action contained in this article if coverage has lapsed.
(Res. No. 07-31, § 1(Exh. A), 6-26-2007; Res. No. 09-12, § 4, 9-14-2009)
1197:
(a) No person shall drive a taxicab without a valid work permit issued pursuant to the requirements of this article. All drivers must have held a valid Georgia driver's license for a minimum period of one continuous year prior to applying for a work permit pursuant to this article. No business shall employ or associate with in any way, including independent contractors, any driver who has not first met the requirements of this article and been issued a valid work permit as authorized by this article.
(b) No work permit shall be issued to any person who is not employed by or represented by an approved business. All work permits shall expire on the drivers' birthday, and shall be renewed annually. A work permit shall only be good for one business which it was obtained for, if a driver works for more than one cab business he/she must have a work permit for each and every business the driver works for.
(c) Work permits must be posted on the dash or sun visor of the vehicle being driven so that it is visible from the passenger area. Businesses under this article are responsible for checking to ensure that each driver has a current work permit in the driver's possession and posted on the dash or sun visor of the vehicle being operated along with a visible vehicle inspection sticker.
(d) No request for a work permit will be processed unless the permit applicant presents a letter on business stationery to the marshal's office from a current business permit holder requesting issuance of a work permit to the named individual. The work permit applicant will further furnish information requested on a form to be provided by the marshal's office and submit to a police clearance consisting of a background investigation or fingerprinting. Work permit applications must meet the following requirements:
(1) Be at least 21 years of age.
(2) Be a citizen of the United States or a legal alien admitted for permanent residence or who has otherwise been granted employment authorization by the United States Immigration and Naturalization Service (who can show proper paperwork therefor).
(3) Possess a current valid State of Georgia driver's license. Such license must not be limited as defined in O.C.G.A. §§ 40-5-58 and 40-5-64.
(4) Exhibit a proficiency with the English language so as to be able to comprehend and interpret traffic signs, issue written receipts to passengers and obey lawful orders of police and others in lawful authority.
(5) Have not been convicted, been on probation, parole, or been imprisoned for a period of ten years previous to the date of application, or for the violation of any of the following offenses of the state, of any other state or of the United States; any felony; driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol; child molestation; criminal solicitation to commit any of these listed offenses; attempts to commit any of these offenses; any crime of violence or theft; any crime of possession, sale or distribution of illegal drugs or moral turpitude. Discharge without court adjudication of guilt pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 42-8-62 shall not disqualify an applicant.
(6) Have not been convicted of three or more moving traffic violations, or one or more mandatory suspensions as defined by Georgia law, within the 18-month period preceding the date of application or renewal of the application. Discharge without court adjudication of guilt pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 42-8-62 shall not disqualify an applicant.
(7) Have not been convicted of reckless driving or vehicular homicide within a three-month period preceding the date of application or renewal of the application. Discharge without court adjudication of guilt pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 42-8-62 shall not disqualify an applicant.
(e) Drivers are responsible for reporting any change in qualifications or other licensing or permitting information previously supplied to the marshal's office within ten days of the change.
(f) Any vehicle purporting to be a taxicab operating within the unincorporated areas of Paulding County shall be in compliance with all of the provisions of this article or shall be deemed to be in violation of this article.
(Res. No. 07-31, § 1(Exh. A), 6-26-2007)
1198:

1199:

1200:
(a) Suspension. For reasons set forth below, an occupation tax certificate, a business permit or a work permit issued under this article may be suspended until these conditions no longer exist:
(1) Failure to maintain all of the general qualifications applicable to the initial issuance of an occupation tax certificate, business permit, or a work permit.
(2) Violation of any part of this article.
(3) For work permits only: have not been convicted of three or more moving traffic violations, or one or more mandatory suspensions as defined by Georgia law, within the 18-month period preceding the date of application or renewal of the application. Discharge without court adjudication of guilt pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 42-8-62 shall not disqualify an applicant.
(4) Allowing the required insurance coverage to lapse, or allowing a vehicle to operate in the unincorporated area of the county without a county inspection sticker.
(b) Suspension for six months. For reasons set forth below, an occupation tax certificate a business permit, or a work permit issued under the article may be suspended for six months:
(1) Charging a fare in excess of those fares on file with the marshal's office or as posted on the taxicab.
(2) Refusing to accept a passenger solely on the basis of race, color, national origin, religious belief, or sex. Operators shall not refuse to accept a passenger unless the passenger is obviously intoxicated or dangerous.
(c) Revocation. An occupation tax certificate, a business permit, or a work permit issued under this article may be revoked where the applicant furnishes fraudulent or untruthful information, or omits information, requested in the application.
(d) An occupation tax certificate, business permit, or work permit may be revoked for a violation of this article. If any permit holder, employee, or independent contractor of a permit holder is found to have violated this article on three or more occasions in a 12-month period, such permit may be revoked.
(e) A permit may be revoked if any driver affiliated in any way with such permit is found to have violated this article on five or more occasions in a 12-month period.
(f) In addition to any other remedies provided by law, the permit holder may also be cited for violating the provisions of this article, and such citation(s) shall be prosecuted in accordance with the requirements of this article in the Magistrate Court of Paulding County.
(g) The requirements of this article shall be in addition to all other taxing, and regulatory provisions of local, state or federal law and shall not authorize violations of any other applicable laws.
(Res. No. 07-31, § 1(Exh. A), 6-26-2007)
